newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Namibian who praised Nazi Hess cleared of race hate.
newsitem.headline: Namibian who praised Nazi Hess cleared of race hate.

text.p: Namibia's High Court has overturned the conviction of an ethnic German who praised Nazi leader Rudolf Hess, and thrown out the hate-speech law she broke, South Africa's Sunday Times reported.

The woman was found guilty of inciting racial hatred after putting an advertisement in the Windhoek Advertiser praising Hess, number three in Adolf Hitler's hierarchy, and saying he, like Jesus, would be a hero if alive today.

But a judge declared the law invalid, saying it went too far in restricting free speech which is guaranteed in the constitution, and approved the appeal by the woman and the newspaper against their conviction two years ago.

The Sunday Times did not give her name or say whether she had been imprisoned, fined or merely cautioned for lauding Hess, who was jailed for life at the Nuremberg war crimes trials after World War Two.
He committed suicide in Berlin's Spandau prison in 1987 while serving his sentence.
Namibia, once German South-West Africa, is still home to many people of German descent. After decades of South African domination, it won independence in 1990.
